purpose: Iloperidone is used to treat schizophrenia in adults. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that aren't there), delusions (false beliefs), and disorganized thinking. It can help you feel more stable and function better in daily life.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to send signals between nerve cells. In schizophrenia, these chemicals can get out of balance. Iloperidone works by blocking certain receptors for these chemicals, helping to bring them back into a healthier balance so your brain works more normally.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly), fast heartbeat, drowsiness or feeling tired, dry mouth, stuffy nose, weight gain, and difficulty falling asleep. These are not all the side effects, so let your pharmacist or doctor know if anything bothers you.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious heart rhythm change called QT prolongation, so tell your doctor if you have heart problems or take other medications that affect the heart. Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis should NOT take this drug due to increased risk of death. It may cause a drop in blood pressure when you stand up, increasing fall risk. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Seek help right away if you have uncontrolled muscle movements, high fever, or stiff muscles.
typical_dosing: You usually start at a very low dose of 1 mg twice a day, and your doctor slowly increases it over about a week to reduce dizziness. The typical target dose is between 6 mg and 12 mg twice daily. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and never change your dose on your own.
